title: U.S. House · Texas's 14th District
area: Southeast Texas along the Gulf Coast, including Galveston, Jefferson and Orange counties.

context.text: Incumbent Republican Randy Weber defeated Jessica Forgy in the Republican primary, 88.6%-11.4%. Thurman Bill Bartie, a former Mayor of Port Arthur, defeated Richard Davis in the May 26, 2026 Democratic primary runoff, 51.0%-49.0%, after the two advanced from a three-candidate March primary.

candidates.name: Randy Weber
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary, 88.6%-11.4%, over Jessica Forgy

summary.text: Randy Weber is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in Texas's 14th District. He founded and ran an air-conditioning company for decades, served on the Pearland City Council and in the Texas House, and was first elected to Congress in 2012. He serves on the Energy and Commerce and Science, Space, and Technology committees, where he chairs the Science Committee's Energy Subcommittee.

background.text: Weber was born in Pearland, Texas, in 1953, and according to his House biography has lived within a 20-mile radius of the Gulf Coast area all his life.
He attended Alvin Community College and earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Houston-Clear Lake, a Bachelor of Science in public affairs in 1977.
He founded Weber's Air & Heat, an air-conditioning company, in 1981 and owned it until 2016.

He served on the Pearland City Council from 1990 to 1996, and was a Brazoria County grand jury commissioner, president of the Brazoria County Cities Association, and chair of the Pearland Area Republican Party Headquarters.

Weber lost a January 2007 special-election runoff for a Texas House seat, then won the seat in 2008 and served in the Texas House until 2012. According to his House biography, he served on the Environmental Regulation and Public Education committees and as vice chair of Border and Intergovernmental Affairs.
According to his House biography, he authored legislation in the Texas House to combat human trafficking.

In 2012 he won an open-seat race for the 14th District after Ron Paul retired, winning the Republican runoff against Felicia Harris and then defeating Democrat Nick Lampson in the general election; he took office in January 2013.

In Congress he serves on the Energy and Commerce Committee (Energy, Environment, and Oversight and Investigations subcommittees) and on the Science, Space, and Technology Committee, where he chairs the Energy Subcommittee; he previously served on the Foreign Affairs and Transportation and Infrastructure committees.
According to his House biography, he is married to Brenda Weber, a retired schoolteacher, and they have three children and eight grandchildren; he is an active member of his church and community.

record.text: Serves on the Committee on Energy and Commerce as Vice Chair of its Subcommittee on Energy, and on its Subcommittees on Oversight and Investigations and Environment, for the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Serves on the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, chairing its Subcommittee on Energy, for the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Thurman Bill Bartie
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 26, 2026 Democratic primary runoff, 51.0%-49.0%, over Richard Davis

summary.text: Thurman Bill Bartie is the Democratic nominee challenging incumbent Randy Weber in Texas's 14th District. A lifelong Port Arthur resident, he has worked as a funeral director, teacher and pastor, was elected Justice of the Peace for Precinct 8 in Jefferson County in 1994, and served two terms as Mayor of Port Arthur. His campaign website lists economic opportunity, education, infrastructure and healthcare among his priorities.

background.text: Bartie is a lifelong resident of Port Arthur, Texas, and graduated from Lincoln High School.
He studied political science at Prairie View A&M University and earned a bachelor's degree from Lamar University.
He studied mortuary science at the Commonwealth College of Mortuary Science and became a licensed funeral director and embalmer.
He earned a master's degree in ministry from Tennessee Temple University Baptist Seminary.
His career experience includes working as a funeral director and embalmer at Hannah Funeral Home, as a teacher at Memorial High School, and as a pastor.
In 1994 he was elected the first African American Justice of the Peace for Precinct 8 in Jefferson County.
In 2019 he was elected Mayor of Port Arthur, defeating incumbent Derrick Freeman in a runoff, and served two terms.
In the 2026 Democratic primary he advanced to a runoff and defeated Richard Davis on May 26, 2026, with 51.0% of the vote.

priorities.text: Economic opportunity: supports small-business growth, fair wages and safe working conditions.
Public education funding: supports fair and equal funding for public schools and opposes dismantling the Department of Education.
Disaster resilience for southeast Texas, citing the district's history of hurricanes, floods, ice storms and periods of very high heat.

positions.summary: Says he supports healthcare access for every American through complete funding of the Affordable Care Act.
